alternative_readings: If outside the retained HTML body means separately supplied, the appendix’s distinct source locator supports that reading. If it means absent from the joined evidence, that reading is contradicted: all three appendix pages are supplied.
References to legislation establish the circular’s stated regulatory framework; they do not reproduce every operative provision or establish formal incorporation of every referenced law.

Part A supplies non-exhaustive considerations, not an exhaustive compliance safe harbour. Part B specifically addresses bearer-form Tokenised Securities using permissionless tokens on public-permissionless networks; paragraph 18’s general cross-reference does not expressly remove that scope limitation.

Part B(f)’s omnibus-client-account exception concerns segregation from other customers’ assets, not segregation from the custodian’s or sub-custodian’s assets. Its custody considerations do not themselves establish a statutory exemption.

Paragraph 26 removes the circular’s rationale for a mandatory PI-only restriction on Tokenised Securities, while paragraph 27 preserves the public-offering regimes and applicable exemptions. It does not establish unrestricted retail distribution.

Official provenance, completeness, relevant-date versions, amendments and supersession remain unverified. Source locators and hashes alone do not establish authenticity, currentness or applicability.
Application requires facts about the intermediary, activity, instrument, governing law, offering audience, authorisations, exemptions, token form, network permissions and custody arrangement.

Other referenced regulatory materials remain external, including the authorised-product circular, online-distribution guidelines, Code of Conduct, joint virtual-asset circular, portfolio-management Terms and Conditions and VATP guidelines. Their relevance and versions require separate assessment.

value.proposition: The original source-gap proposition requires qualification. On inspection of the whole supplied circular and three-page appendix, the appendix is separately retained and joined to this packet; it is not missing from the supplied evidence, although its contents are outside the main circular’s retained body. Paragraphs 14, 15 and 18 expressly refer to its Parts A and B. Part A addresses vendor experience, technical and legal risks, continuity, privacy and AML/CFT; Part B adds custody considerations for the specified bearer-form, permissionless-token arrangement. The referenced legislative provisions themselves remain absent: the circular identifies or summarises legislation without supplying its complete operative text. Thus the appendix-content gap is resolved within this packet, but the requirement for each relevant official legislative provision, and any conclusion about current applicability, remains unresolved. This is a source-answer proposal, not legal proof.
